titleStmt.title: History of the Zhou Dynasty · Western Zhou 西周

div.p: The first years after the conquest of Shang, about 1046 to 1036 BC: King Wu's settlement of the royal domain of Yin Shang and his enfeoffments; the Duke of Zhou's regency, the rising of Guan, Cai and Wu Geng and the three years of the eastern campaign; the founding of Yan (燕) and the fall of Yan (奄) and Pugu; and the moving of the people of Yin to Luoyi, the Zhouyuan and Feng and Hao.

The cultures appearing in the same span, about the beginning of the Western Zhou: the Upper Xiajiadian and Shi'ertaiyingzi cultures; the Baode type; the Lanqiao–Xujianian type of the Siwa culture; and the Xituanshan, Baoshan and Tanheli cultures and the Wanfabozi remains.

From the end of the Duke of Zhou's regency to the reign of King Kang, about 1036 to 1000 BC: the Duke of Zhou's death and burial at Bi; the move of Tangshu Yu's house from Tang to Jin; Yan's reach into western Liaoning; King Kang's wars against the Dongyi, the Earl of Chu and the Hufang; and the "Good Governance of Cheng and Kang".

The reigns of King Zhao and King Mu, about 1000 to 950 BC: King Zhao's southern campaigns against Jing and the loss of the six armies in the Han; King Mu in the Shiji, the Bamboo Annals and the Mu Tianzi Zhuan; and the Huaiyi and the Nanyi in the bronze inscriptions of King Mu's time.

The cultures appearing in the same span, about 1000 BC: the final period of the Xindian culture and Phase V of the Kayue culture; and in Korea, the Upper Misong-ri culture and Phase II of the Geumtan-ri Bronze Age culture.

The later reign of King Mu and the reign of King Gong, about 950 to 900 BC: King Mu's wars with the Huaiyi and the eastern states in the Ban gui, and Dong's fight at Hu; Yu's campaigns against the Guifang in the Yu ding; the little that is recorded of war under King Gong; and the accession of King Yi (懿).
